runtime_release.provenance_note: The binary's baked OCTOS_GIT_SHA (crates/octos-cli/build.rs: `git rev-parse HEAD`) is 7a79c5bc656886e8b3a5b55f58d0ee5851537d96, which is NOT a commit of this repository; that object does not exist here and no branch contains it. The short hash in the version string (7a79c5b) is that commit's first seven characters. release-metadata.txt records the tag commit 426f6a8e… instead, so the release was published from a working copy whose HEAD was 7a79c5bc…. `octos arc run --lock` compares source_commit against the binary's OCTOS_GIT_SHA, so the machine-checked field carries the value the artifact actually reports and the tag commit is kept beside it; writing the tag commit there instead is verified to fail the pin check. The build tree was clean (see verified_by.source_dirty), so the only remaining gap is that commit itself: it is not reachable from any published branch, which is what makes this release non-reproducible from the repository. A rebuild published from a committed revision is what would close that.

verified_by.how: Downloaded octos-bundle-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz (62,487,625 B) and recomputed both digests locally; both match the published bundle.sha256 / octos.sha256 and release-metadata.txt. source_commit was read out of the extracted ELF as a 40-hex constant adjacent to the baked OCTOS_BUILD_TARGET string, not copied from the release notes. The whole manifest was then verified by the real binary: running `octos arc <req> --output-dir <dir> --mode create --runtime-lock <this file>` (without --prepare-only, which returns before pin::verify) reached the stage after the pin check and stopped at 'Set --model or MODEL' (runner.rs:475). Substituting only the tag commit for source_commit under the same conditions fails at pin.rs:68 'Runtime source commit mismatch', so the pin check really did run and accept these values.
verified_by.source_dirty_evidence: pin::verify refuses a binary built from tracked uncommitted changes, and in the run above it did not refuse: the failure came from the later model-configuration stage, so OCTOS_SOURCE_DIRTY was baked as "false" and the release came from a clean tree.
unverified: provenance of commit 7a79c5bc656886e8b3a5b55f58d0ee5851537d96 (absent from this repository, so the build tree cannot be reconstructed from here)
